intent_snapshot.goal: Make loop steering act on the item's ULS batch: abandon runs discardLanes (gated stop, closeWithProof, per-child Lane and imm-lane removal, imm/<slug> deletion once every Lane is removed, terminal discarded record, batch_lane_retained with a named condition and retry otherwise), pause skips advanceLanes for the item's batch, and resume observes first and exempts one stall judgment, per D4 of docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md.

acceptance.assertion: Source BR-DEC-A4, BR-SCN-A3; meet D4.1-D4.2 in docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-leader-steering.test.ts, tests/session-lane-cleanup.test.ts. Done looks like: abandoning an item with an active two-child batch stops and proof-closes both fake sessions, removes both imm-lane/ branches and their worktrees and imm/<slug>, marks the record discarded with a report, and imm-loop status shows the item abandoned. Negative: a session whose [imm:<session_key>] ownership does not match is not closed and its Lane and imm/<slug> are retained with batch_lane_retained naming the condition; a dirty child worktree is retained; the next tick retries only the retained parts; Host retire_stale_batch is unchanged.

Source BR-DEC-A4; meet D4.3 in docs/specs/loop-leader-uls-alignment.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-leader-steering.test.ts. Done looks like: while the item is paused, ticks call no advanceLanes for its batch and the child session generation and no_progress are unchanged; after resume, an idle session at the unchanged baseline is not closed or rotated on the first tick and is judged by the normal parent_relayed rule on the second. Negative: an exited session observed on the first tick after resume is still handled as exited.

intent_snapshot.scope_size_reason: discardLanes, the discarded record state and the steering hook that triggers it must land together so an abandoned item never leaves a running batch; pause and resume share the same per-tick advance gate.

attestations.summary: S4-AC1: discardAbandonedBatches/discardBatchLanes stop+closeWithProof each child, retain not_owned/unusable-provider/dirty Lanes with batch_lane_retained, delete imm/<slug> only after every Lane is gone, write discarded report, leave terminal records untouched; S4-AC2: driveGate skips paused items without spending deadlines, relayed advance skips paused, resume_pending yields one stall exemption that holds idle/done but not exited sessions; antigravity runtime tree proven identical to source. Blast radius medium: batch_state.ts persisted shape (new discarding/discarded states, discard field), batch_lanes.ts, child_session_reconciler.ts, loop_daemon tick.

advisory_findings.summary: An in-flight drive advance that passed driveGate before abandon can write the batch record back after discardBatchLanes set discarding, dropping the discard progress; the next tick then re-calls closeWithProof on already-closed handles of removed children, which a provider may refuse and retain indefinitely.

evidence.trigger: standing daemon: drive job advanceLanes running while the tick's discardAbandonedBatches writes batch_state discarding → advance persists its in-memory record (running, no discard) → next tick revisits removed children and calls closeWithProof on closed handles → possible permanent batch_lane_retained

advisory_findings.summary: A child session with a key but no handle whose find returns not_found is removed with proof null (treated as never holding a session); no test pins this path.

evidence.trigger: child.session.key set, handle null, port.find → {ok:true,not_found:true} → cleanupDiscardedChildLane runs with proof null and removes the Lane without an exit proof
